distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. We need an adverb to describe how the action of sleeping is done, so we say 'sleep well'.
'Fine' is informal and is not used to describe how someone sleeps. We don't say 'sleep fine'.
'Nice' is an adjective used to describe things or people. We don't say 'sleep nice'.

l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często stawiają przysłówek przed czasownikiem, mówiąc 'well sleep' zamiast poprawnego 'sleep well'.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb in this kind of collocation. 'Well' describes how the action is done, so it follows 'sleep'.

related_collocations.example: The old dog walks slowly in the garden.
The dog barks loudly when the mail arrives.
The horse eats quickly after a long run.

memory_tip: WELL = an adverb that describes how someone sleeps (sleep well) | GOOD = an adjective that describes a noun (a good dog)
